chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Shu'ayb ibn Abdillah from one of his companions, raising it, said:

A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said, 'O Commander of the Faithful! Advise me of an aspect of righteousness by which I may attain salvation.' The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'O questioner! Listen, then understand, then be convinced, then act; and know that people are of three types: an ascetic, a patient one, and a covetous one.'
As for the ascetic, grief and happiness have exited his heart, so he does not rejoice in anything from the world, nor does he despair over anything from it that has left him; thus he is at peace.

As for the patient one, he wishes for it in his heart; but when he attains from it, he restrains his self from it due to its evil consequence and its repulsiveness. If you were to look into his heart, you would be astonished by its chastity, humility, and resoluteness.

As for the covetous one, he does not care from where the world comes to him, whether from its permissible means or its prohibited means, and he does not care what filth he has incurred in it, destroyed his soul, and lost his manliness; thus they are in a flood of confusion, tossing about.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful; title for Imam Ali
key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: The world; worldly life and its pleasures
key_terms.رَاغِبٌ: Covetous; one who eagerly seeks worldly gain regardless of source
key_terms.زَاهِدٌ: Ascetic; one who has detached from worldly emotions
key_terms.صَابِرٌ: Patient; one who restrains self-desire despite longing

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of people according to Imam Ali in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi presents a nuanced tripartite classification of human spiritual states, distinguishing between the ascetic (zāhid) who has transcended worldly attachment, the patient (ṣābir) who controls desire through foresight of the Hereafter, and the covetous (rāhib) who pursues worldly gain indiscriminately. Scholarly commentary often highlights this as a practical guide for self-assessment, emphasizing that true righteousness requires not just action but the purification of the heart's relationship with the transient world. The opening instruction to 'listen, ask, be convinced, then act' underscores the Shia epistemological emphasis on verified knowledge preceding practice.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Shuayb Bin Abdullah, from one of his companions, raising it, said,

‘A man came over to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> and he said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>! Advise me of an aspect from the aspects of the righteousness I can attain salvation with it’. Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O you questioner! Listen intently, then understand, then be convinced, and perform; and know that the people are three (types) – an ascetic, and a patient, and a coveting one (having cravings).

So as for the ascetic one, so the grief and the happiness has exited from his heart, so he does not get happy with anything from the world nor does he despair upon anything that is lost from him. Thus he is in peace (of mind).

And as for the patient one, so he wishes for it in his heart. So when he does attain from it, reins (restraints) his self from it due to the evil consequences of it and its seduction. Were you to be notified upon (the contents of) his heart it would astonish you from its chastity, and its humbleness, and its resoluteness.

And as for the covetous one, so he does not care from when the world comes to him, from its Permissible (means) or from its Prohibited (means), and he does not care what filth there is in its display, and it destroys his soul, and removes his honour. Thus, these (covetous ones) are in the midst of disturbances’.
en.sarwar: 13. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Shu’ayb ibn ‘Abd Allah from certain individuals of his people in a marfu’ manner that has said the following:

“Once a man came to Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) and said, ‘O Amir al- Mu’minin, grant me good advice in the aspects of virtue so I may attain salvation.’ Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) said, ‘O seeker of advice, listen carefully, understand, ascertain and practice. You must know that people are of three kinds: restraining themselves from worldly matters, exercising patience and those who are inclined toward worldly gains.

“From the hearts of restraining people sadness and happiness have moved out. He does not become happy for any of the worldly things, nor he is grieved over anything of the world that he may have missed, thus, he is comfortable.

“The person who exercises patience has hopes to have worldly gains in his heart and when he gains anything he holds his soul back from it due to such gains’ bad consequences and disgrace. Were you to see his heart you would be astonished by its chastity, humility and determination.

“To those who are inclined to worldly gains it does not matter wherefrom worldly gains come to them, lawful or unlawful as well as whether it throws filth over their honor or destroys their souls, or takes away their kindness. They are restless in a vortex. ’”
